summary: Unexpected elevation of 5xx errors caused by kv-cache lock contention + proxy throttling during large embedding upload
description: Issue summary: During a customer bulk embedding upload window (evening US-East heavy usage), we observed an abrupt elevation in 5xx responses from the API gateway to the customer’s requests. Impact: Customer reported ~20% of embedding upload requests returning 502/503, causing failed batches and retries. Several downstream services reported elevated latencies and partial timeouts. Environment: prod-us-east-1, dedicated tenant for DataCanvas Inc. Observed at approx 2026-03-13T23:10:00Z and sustained for ~40 minutes. Initial symptom: sudden rise in api-gateway 5xx rate from baseline ~1% to a peak ~18% correlated with a large multipart embedding upload from the customer. Key error types: 502 Bad Gateway, 503 Service Unavailable, and internal runtime 5xx from serving-runtime.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) On prod-us-east-1, as tenant 'datacanvas' begin a concurrent multipart embedding upload of ~1200 records in small batches (size=16).
2) Trigger steady traffic to other tenants to emulate normal evening load (50% baseline).
3) Observe apigw metrics: 5xx rate, upstream latency, and proxy connection resets.
4) Watch serving-runtime / kvcache metrics for lock wait times, queue lengths, and evictions.
investigation_notes: Initial triage by support: customer bulk upload timeline matches error onset; retries amplify connection churn at apigw.
SRE observation: kvcache lock wait spikes preceded runtime threadpool starvation events; many prefetch workers blocked on kvcache writes.
Hypothesis A: Large parallel embedding prefetches are serializing on a kvcache shard lock, causing long tail waits and tying up runtime threads which leads to proxy timeouts and apigw 502s.
Hypothesis B: Edge proxy accept-queue reached its soft limit due to retry bursts; proxy begins shedding, causing upstream resets seen as 502 at the gateway.
Checked autoscaler: no GPU OOMs, no node reboots; CPU threads at runtime were saturated (~95%) on shard-serving processes.
Cross-check against logs: several tenants experienced transient increases in kvcache contention but only the dedicated tenant with heavy embedding upload hit the 5xx floor.
Related historical issues: similar kvcache lock amplification seen during large prefetch windows in SUP-813246 note; sharing runbook link for mitigation steps.
comments: Maya Chen (Support) 2026-03-14T00:05Z: Customer reported failing embedding batches and included their upload manifest. Asked for request IDs and timestamps.

Diego Alvarez (SRE) 2026-03-14T00:38Z: Confirmed kvcache lock_wait spike and runtime thread exhaustion. Beginning mitigation plan: reduce concurrent prefetch workers for that tenant as a short-term measure.
Customer (DataCanvas) 2026-03-14T01:12Z: Provided exact upload pattern: 75 parallel connections with aggressive retry on failures. They can throttle concurrency if needed.
Diego Alvarez (SRE) 2026-03-14T01:45Z: Applied temporary tenant-level concurrency cap and increased apigw accept-queue threshold; monitoring for improvement.
mitigation: 1) Applied tenant concurrency cap: limit parallel embedding upload connections to 20 for datacanvas - immediate impact observed on 5xx rate.
2) Temporarily reduced prefetch worker pool size on affected serving-runtime shard to avoid lock amplification.
3) Increased edge-proxy soft accept-queue limit by 20% to give graceful drain buffer during retries.
Observed effect: apigw 5xx rate decreased from ~18% to ~2.5% within 6 minutes of mitigations.
next_steps: Short term: Keep tenant cap and prefetch worker reduction until scheduled maintenance window. Coordinate with customer to shift large uploads to off-peak or use rate-limited bulk API.
Medium term: Implement kvcache sharding rebalancing for high-concurrency upload patterns to reduce single-shard lock hotspots.
Medium term: Add heuristics to detect tenant-driven prefetch storms and apply adaptive backpressure at the prefetcher before runtime threads are exhausted.
Follow-up: Create a post-incident runbook entry with concrete thresholds and automated mitigations; link PR to serving-runtime for safer kvcache writes.
